heroHeadline: RSF Drones Hit Khartoum for First Time in Months as UN Warns of El Fasher-Style Atrocity Risk in Besieged El Obeid
heroSubtitle: Drones struck Khartoum, Atbara, and El-Damer at dawn on August 12, 2026, ending months of relative calm in the capital since its 2025 recapture — a strike following Hemedti's late-July vow to escalate operations after RSF setbacks in North Kordofan. The capital strikes came days after UN experts warned on August 7 that besieged El Obeid faces a real risk of large-scale atrocities echoing the RSF's 2025 El Fasher massacre, citing near-constant drone strikes (up to 40 aircraft overhead at once), a worsening cholera outbreak, and critical water shortages. In West Darfur, SAF-allied Joint Force fighters twice repelled RSF assaults on the strategic Bir Saliba area (August 4 and 8), killing RSF field commander Mahdi Adam ('Jebel Moon') in the first attempt, while the fighting displaced over 6,650 people from 11 nearby villages. Separately, a drone strike on a tribal court gathering in Garra al-Zawaya, North Darfur, killed at least 35 people on August 2, including four tribal leaders and two RSF commanders — Emergency Lawyers Sudan attributed the strike to SAF drones. Day 1216 of the SAF-RSF war with no ceasefire and famine conditions persisting across Darfur and Kordofan.
